resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.whatWasAttempted: admitting a RepairPlanDescriptor whose permittedEditScope is `src/**` against an edit to `src/legacy.js`, and selecting rule subjects with include globs.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.whatTheKitSays: the alphabet is closed and ONE semantic fact is published: `**/*.ts` matches root `a.ts`, i.e. a LEADING `**/` may match ZERO segments. Nothing states what a TRAILING `**` matches.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.mathematicalCorrectionToThisOriginsV16Ra: the v16 write-up said "Under 'zero or more segments' `src/**` matches `src/` only; under 'one or more' it matches `src/legacy.js`". The first clause is WRONG as stated: a zero-or-more set CONTAINS the nonzero lengths, so a zero-or-more reading of `src/**` matches `src/`, `src/legacy.js` AND `src/a/b.js`. Correcting that arithmetic does NOT dissolve the underspecification, and the two are kept separate here.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.whyItIsNotAlgorithmFreedom: permittedEditScope decides whether a repair edit is admissible, and policy include/exclude decides subject enumeration and therefore which findings exist. Both are normative outcomes.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.whatTheLoneExampleLOGICALLYFORCES: exactly one thing, and it is about a LEADING `**/`: since `**/*.ts` matches root `a.ts`, the token sequence `**/` must be able to consume ZERO segments (the `**` together with its following separator may elide). The example says nothing about a `**` that has no following separator, because it contains none. A trailing-`**` rule therefore cannot be DERIVED from it in either direction.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.oneInterpretationThatExplainsTheExample: read `**` as a SEGMENT-GROUP that is always followed by a separator, the separator included in the group and the group allowed to be empty. That account explains the published example, and under it a TRAILING `**` -- with no following segment -- matches a path only if the path ends at a separator, so `src/**` matches NO file. This is presented as a POSSIBLE interpretation that is consistent with the example, not as what the example forces.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.aDifferentInterpretationAlsoConsistent: read a trailing `**` as "any remaining suffix". That reading also satisfies the closed alphabet and the same published example, and under it `src/**` matches every descendant file.
resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.thereforeTheGap: the two readings agree on the one published example and DISAGREE on whether the same repair plan and the same subject set are admissible. The gap is not which reading is right: it is that the kit does not say, and that nothing in the kit forces either answer.

resolvedByANormativeSuccessor.smallestFix: one sentence, or a second published example with a trailing `**`.
